items.summary: The US House of Representatives officially nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (New York) to be Speaker, positioning him to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber and preside over his party's largest House majority in years. The election is scheduled for 3 January when Democrats take control following a midterm sweep; as of Wednesday they hold at least 257 seats, well beyond the 218 needed for a majority, though seven races remain uncalled. Jeffries was re-elected party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday and has served as minority leader since 2023; he called the nomination "a high honour and a distinct privilege." Despite overwhelming support, several left-wing holdouts voiced reservations: seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement that more work is needed to ensure the party's direction reflects constituents' demands. The Congressional Progressive Caucus congratulated Jeffries but pledged to continue conversations about delivering "a bold agenda for working people." Looking ahead, Democrats anticipate clashes with President Donald Trump, who has signalled willingness to cooperate on some issues while pledging to use his veto power; this could complicate efforts to address affordability and pass reforms. At a news conference following the vote, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing" and "make healthcare affordable for every single American." Even with a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries faces sharp internal ideological divisions over US support of Israel and rising healthcare costs. Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won by challenging the party establishment. As Speaker, he will also manage investigations into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that Democrats control oversight powers. Rounding out leadership, House Democrats elected Katherine Clark (Massachusetts) as majority leader, Pete Aguilar (California) as majority whip, and Joe Neguse (Colorado) as assistant speaker.
items.title: Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries as Speaker of the House

items.summary: Officials at Grand Canyon National Park announced Wednesday that they are easing water restrictions after reaching a milestone in restoring the region's water service, allowing overnight guests to return to several lodges on the South Rim. The famous El Tovar Hotel and other lodges will reopen Friday following severe flooding earlier this year. Late-August flooding caused three deaths, prompted rescues, and damaged key infrastructure including a water intake pump and a significant stretch of a decades-old pipeline that supplied water for millions of visitors to the South Rim and about 1,600 residents of Grand Canyon Village. At the time of the damage, officials said they were just over a month away from completing a more than $200 million upgrade to the 12.5-mile-long (20-kilometer) Transcanyon Waterline; additional flooding in September then damaged temporary repairs. Although lodging is reopening, park officials urge visitors to conserve water as restoration of the system continues, advising shorter showers, turning off faucets when not in use, and avoiding unnecessary water use. Food and beverage services will resume gradually according to park officials. A banner image of the Grand Canyon was credited to Amy Martin via National Park Service. The article provides no further details on timelines for completing the full restoration or specific reopening schedules beyond Friday for lodging.
items.title: Grand Canyon South Rim hotels reopen as park eases water restrictions

items.summary: Employees have reported a new round of layoffs at Intel's global IT team, with accounts circulating this week and describing job losses within the chipmaker. Some employees said they were told their positions were being eliminated, though the number of jobs affected and the locations involved remain unclear as of writing. An Intel spokesperson responded that the company continually assesses its workforce to align priorities and resources as part of a broader strategy to become more focused and efficient; however, the statement gave no headcount or list of affected teams and did not explicitly confirm a new round of layoffs. The reports come as CEO Lip-Bu Tan continues to streamline operations and reduce costs, with Intel entering the final quarter of 2026 with 4,000 fewer employees than at the end of 2025. One anonymous post on an employee discussion forum claimed the cuts affected a double-digit percentage of Intel's IT workforce, but it provided no headcount and remains unverified. Separately, between July and October, Intel filed nine notices in California under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (WARN), which requires employers to report certain layoffs; those notices covered 222 employees, including workers at facilities in Santa Clara. The most recent notice reportedly listed 67 permanent layoffs at Intel's Folsom campus, effective October 31, and as of November 17 California public records showed no newer Intel notice. These filings offer a limited view of the reported IT cuts because smaller reductions may fall below reporting thresholds and overseas jobs are outside California's jurisdiction. On an enterprise-wide basis, Intel reported 81,100 employees as of September 26, including 76,500 at Intel and 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries; the total was down from 85,100 at the end of 2025 and 88,400 a year earlier. The article is based on reporting by CTech, which noted that figures involving employees remain unverified where not otherwise confirmed through official filings or disclosures.
items.title: Intel reports new IT layoffs amid ongoing workforce reduction

items.summary: The Nvidia controversy over alleged illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China has acquired a personal, Indian-American angle involving Jay Puri, the company's former worldwide sales chief and once its third-ranking executive. The connection is familial rather than professional: Puri's wife, Cenly Chen, was a senior Super Micro Computer (Supermicro) executive charged by US prosecutors with conspiring to smuggle $2.5 billion worth of servers containing Nvidia chips to Chinese customers. Technology publication The Information reported Wednesday that Puri and Chen had told colleagues about their marriage this year, noting that Chen managed Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia—though the company has disputed her alleged role in chip allocations. This development followed a Tuesday report by Muddy Waters Research, an influential short-selling firm founded in 2010 by American investor Carson Block, which disclosed it was shorting Nvidia shares and raised questions about the Puri-Chen relationship. The report, titled NVIDIA: More China, cited photographs from 2024 to 2026 showing Puri alongside a woman identified variously as Cenly Chen and Cenly Puri. It relied on an October shareholder lawsuit alleging that Chen "managed SMCI's acquisition of GPU chips from NVIDIA" and "decided how to distribute NVDA GPUs among Super Micro's customers," going further to allege there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge" of the illicit sales. However, Chen has not been charged with any criminal offence, her allegations remain unproven, Supermicro denies she managed its Nvidia relationship or controlled GPU distribution, and Puri has not been accused of wrongdoing. The report's timing coincided with Muddy Waters' financial interest in a declining Nvidia share price; the firm made its reputation exposing alleged accounting fraud at Sino-Forest by publishing investigative reports while taking positions in scrutinized shares. Puri, 71, is described as a veteran Silicon Valley executive whose career spans nearly five decades: an electrical engineering graduate of the University of Minnesota with master's degrees from Caltech and Harvard Business School; he spent 22 years at Sun Microsystems—holding senior roles including head of its Asia-Pacific operations—and previously worked at Hewlett-Packard, Booz Allen Hamilton and Texas Instruments. At Nvidia he became executive vice-president of Worldwide Field Operations in 2009, overseeing global sales, business development, partnerships and customer relationships; he announced his retirement from that operational role in June but remains a senior adviser, though his association with the company has not always been harmonious—media reports citing insiders claim Jensen Huang once berated Puri during a closed-door February meeting attended by more than 30 executives. The scandal unfolds against an increasingly charged American political climate marked by suspicion of foreign connections, particularly Chinese ones, even as Silicon Valley remains built on international talent, with Indian-origin executives including Satya Nadella of Microsoft, Sundar Pichai of Alphabet and Arvind Krishna of IBM leading major corporations. Separately, Nvidia's crisis has escalated: chairman Harvey Jones delivered a decisive rebuff to pressure to reinstate Huang as CEO, saying the board had unanimously accepted his resignation and "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," while Huang is expected to face congressional questioning on December 1.
items.title: Nvidia's China chip-diversion scandal gains an Indian-American dimension through former sales chief Jay Puri and his wife Cenly Chen of Supermicro

items.summary: India's central bank warned that a Supreme Court ruling reversing the write-off of bonds issued by troubled lender Yes Bank could undermine bank rescue rules, according to a court filing reviewed by Reuters. The dispute stems from Yes Bank's 2020 rescue when authorities wrote off Rs8,415 crore worth of additional Tier-1 (AT1) bonds, securities designed to absorb losses during banking distress. In a November 13 filing, the Reserve Bank of India argued that the apex court ruling conflicts with loss-absorption provisions under international Basel banking regulations and could harm Yes Bank's existing depositors. The arguments appeared in a review petition not publicly available, and neither the RBI nor Yes Bank responded to Reuters requests for comment. Last month the Supreme Court ruled the write-off illegal over procedural lapses and ordered the bonds restored, though review petitions by the bank and RBI have delayed relief for investors. In its filing, the RBI argued that writing down or converting AT1 bonds was inevitable under India's rescue framework and that letting them survive a restructuring would defeat their loss-absorbing purpose. Quoting the regulator: 'The effect of the impugned judgment thus defeats the mandatory loss-absorption requirement of AT-1 Bonds and renders the relevant provisions of the Basel III Master Circular otiose.' The RBI also warned the ruling could have wider implications for India's bank rescue framework, noting regulations and bond terms already required AT1 bonds to be written down even without an explicit provision in the restructuring plan. Restoring Rs8,414 crore ($900.52 million) in liabilities would dilute capital injected by State Bank of India and other rescue investors and weaken depositor protections, per the RBI. The regulator also rejected the court's characterization of it as a 'mere bystander' during Yes Bank's collapse, asserting it repeatedly pushed the lender to raise capital, appointed an additional director, and ultimately intervened when the bank became insolvent. Published November 18, 2026.
items.title: RBI warns Yes Bank AT1 bond write-off reversal could undermine bank rescue rules

items.summary: On Tuesday in Mumbai, the WhatsApp account of Thane Police Commissioner Ashutosh Dumbre was reportedly hacked. Around 4:45 pm, approximately 20 obscene videos were uploaded to his WhatsApp status. The breach ran for nearly two hours before it came under control; all objectionable videos had been removed by around 6 pm. A case was registered against an unidentified person at the Cyber Police Station and subsequently transferred to the Maharashtra Nodal Cyber Unit for investigation, though police sources said the case-related documents have not yet been formally handed over to that unit. The Crime Branch and Cyber Cell immediately began efforts to contain the breach once the videos were noticed on the Commissioner's status. In response, the Thane Police Commissionerate issued a public advisory urging citizens not to view, download, share or forward the objectionable videos from the compromised account. Senior Police Inspector Shailesh Salvi, Public Relations Officer of the Thane Police Commissionerate, delivered the advisory and appealed for cooperation. The police also cautioned people against responding to suspicious messages or clicking on links received from the account, warned citizens not to believe or circulate content posted on the WhatsApp status, and advised against spreading rumours about the incident. A promotional property-deal link appears appended to the item's text but is unrelated to the reported hack; no names of suspects were disclosed.
items.title: Thane Police Commissioner's WhatsApp Account Hacked; ~20 Obscene Videos Uploaded to Status

items.summary: The board of directors of Nvidia Corporation has refused to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, a decision made despite support from US President Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and thousands of employees and investors. The editorial frames this refusal as an affirmation of corporate governance principles—accountability and succession planning—and asserts that no individual can be placed above the institution he helped build. While acknowledging Huang's extraordinary contributions under which Nvidia became one of the world's most valuable companies, the piece argues that leadership requires more than technological brilliance, commercial success, or personal charisma; it demands trust. The controversy is described as extending beyond Huang's extramarital relationships, which are characterized as belonging primarily to the private sphere. Instead, the article identifies his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence authorities of having links to Chinese intelligence—and alleged diversion of restricted American AI chips to China—as the far more consequential issue. It contends that trust is painstakingly built over decades but can be seriously damaged by a single lapse in judgment, and once lost, rebuilding it is extraordinarily difficult. The editorial then raises whether Nvidia possesses sufficient leadership depth to prosper without Huang. At 63, Huang is described as not too old to lead the company, yet the piece argues that a corporation of Nvidia's size and strategic importance should never become excessively dependent on one individual, since strong institutions cultivate successors, distribute responsibilities, and establish management systems capable of surviving unexpected departures. Colette Kress is named as interim chief executive offering continuity; if the board believes Nvidia needs a new CEO, Huang should respect that decision. As co-founder and largest shareholder, he can nominate two directors to the board and guide his successor. The article concludes by defining the ultimate measure of his legacy as an institution capable of thriving without him, asserting that great leaders build great companies while truly exceptional leaders ensure those companies outlast their leadership.
items.title: Nvidia Board Refuses to Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Leadership Controversy

items.summary: In Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon around 1:30 pm, an actress named Simran Kawaljeet Singh Rana (30), a resident of Andheri West who works as an actress and appears in promotional reels for various companies, lost her handbag while shooting promotional Instagram reels for a skincare brand at Carter Road in Bandra West. The bag reportedly contained makeup products worth approximately ₹25,000—including lipstick, mascara, kajal, lip gloss, foundation, concealer, moisturiser, and sunscreen—along with clothes, footwear, a white mobile phone charger, earphones, and keys collectively valued around ₹15,000, plus a wallet holding ₹3,500 in cash. The complainant had initially kept the bag inside the company's car during the shoot. When she needed her makeup products, team member Kareena Atre brought the bag from the car but allegedly placed it on a concrete seating platform near the seashore beside Carter Road Police Chowky without informing Rana. After completing the shoot, when Rana asked about the handbag and was told it had been left on the platform, she discovered that by the time the team went to retrieve it, the bag was missing. The team searched the surrounding area but could not locate it. Suspecting an unidentified person had stolen the handbag along with its contents, Rana approached Khar Police Station and lodged a complaint. According to the FIR, police have registered a case against an unidentified person and are investigating the matter.
items.title: Mumbai Actress Loses Handbag Worth ₹43,500 During Instagram Reel Shoot in Bandra West

items.summary: In the July-September quarter, Apple's iPhone shipments declined 25% year-on-year to approximately 3.7 million units, down from a record 5 million units in the same period a year earlier, IDC data reported by The Times of India (ToI). The contraction pushed Apple into fourth place among smartphone brands in India, though several rivals recorded sharper declines. Samsung was the only top-10 brand to grow shipments, rising 7.9% as its market share expanded from 12.6% to 17.7%. Oppo held third despite a 26.5% contraction. IDC attributed Apple's decline to supply shortages across the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 ranges, reduced discounts on older models, and price increases around the September launch. India's overall smartphone shipments fell 23.3% to 36.8 million units in the quarter, marking the weakest festive quarter in a decade; rising memory chip costs pushed prices higher and limited discounting ability, prompting retailers to hold back fresh orders. Offline channel shipments dropped 26.7%, versus an 18.9% fall online, while the sub-$100 segment contracted sharply by 90.9% to 700,000 units, with its share shrinking from 16.2% to 1.9%. Despite lower volumes, average selling price rose 26.1% to a record $371, while overall market value fell 3.3%. Upasana Joshi, senior research manager at IDC Asia Pacific, said higher prices, thin discounts and longer replacement cycles kept demand subdued through the festive period. IDC expects the downturn to intensify in October-December, forecasting more than 25% year-on-year shipment decline as cheaper-handset inventories dwindle. For 2026, it projects total smartphone shipments of 125-127 million units, a 16-18% drop from 2025 levels. The report draws on inputs from ToI's Aabhas Sharma and is published by The Economic Times.
items.title: Apple's India iPhone shipments fall sharply as Samsung grows in festive quarter

items.summary:
Spot gold fell 3% to $3,736.06 an ounce at 11:43 a.m. ET after touching $3,734.76 earlier in the session, its lowest level since September 26, 2025. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.2% to $3,739 an ounce. The metal fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 and was heading toward a third consecutive session of losses.

Naeem Aslam, chief investment officer at Zaye Capital Markets, told Reuters that “the selloff reflects mounting pressure from a strengthening US dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of further monetary tightening,” noting that recent economic figures reinforced this sentiment. The dollar rose to a fresh 19-month high as hawkish remarks from Fed officials and recent data strengthened expectations of an interest-rate increase next month.

According to the CME FedWatch tool, markets see a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December and an 8% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move. They are also pricing in quarter-point increases in January and by April. Expectations of tighter policy have pushed the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield toward its longest stretch above 5% in nearly two decades, raising the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets such as gold.

The stronger dollar also makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, told Bloomberg that “it is a tough environment for gold,” and said the market would remain cautious without a clear catalyst for a reversal.

Gold has lost more than a quarter of its value since the US-Iran war began in late February. The conflict pushed energy prices higher, fueled inflation, and prompted central banks to tighten monetary policy. Investors are now awaiting minutes from the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting for further clues about the rate path. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided directly addressing monetary policy earlier this week, consistent with his stated preference not to provide near-term rate guidance.

Aslam added that “if the minutes reinforce concerns about persistent inflation and support additional tightening, Treasury yields and the dollar could strengthen further, potentially extending gold’s decline below $3,800.”

Other precious metals also fell sharply. Spot silver declined 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce after touching its lowest level since September 26, 2025. Platinum dropped 4.6% to $1,363.50 after hitting its lowest level since September 17, 2025, extending its year-to-date loss to 33%. Palladium fell 2.6% to $945.95, its lowest level since early November.

The article is based on inputs from agencies and does not represent the views of The Economic Times.
items.title: Gold Falls 3% to One-Year Low as Hawkish Fed Sentiment Strengthens Dollar and Yields

items.summary: On Wednesday, OpenAI introduced two new artificial intelligence models: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. The company said both deliver better results while using fewer output tokens. GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for coding on the "hardest projects" as well as scientific work, whereas GPT-6.2 Sol targets everyday tasks. OpenAI stated it trained GPT-6.2 Astra to produce clearer and better-designed slides, spreadsheets, and documents in fields such as law, sales, finance, and accounting, and that it writes cleaner code and builds stronger frontends for websites, gaming, and 3D design. The company also said GPT-6.2 Sol is smarter than GPT-6.1 Sol and lets users complete more tasks under the same paid plan; OpenAI described it as powering through multistep agentic workflows while writing clearly and naturally and being intuitive to collaborate with. On performance, OpenAI reported that GPT-6.2 Astra scored 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra on its benchmarks while costing less than a third as much, and scored 5.5 points higher than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 while costing just 5% as much. On scientific work specifically, the company said GPT-6.2 Astra scored 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost. Regarding pricing in the API, OpenAI stated that GPT-6.2 Astra's input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra's, with a 60% discount on cached input, listing $8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output per million tokens; it added that GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's API token prices. OpenAI concluded by noting that on several benchmarks both models come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.
items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol AI Models

items.summary: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde defended Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC on Wednesday, backing her amid allegations that she tore a photograph of the late Balasaheb (Bal Thackeray). Speaking to news agency ANI, Shinde said he had personally seen the photograph and asserted that 'the torn portion of the picture showed Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar's face,' adding that 'Shaina NC has already provided a clarification.' He reiterated that any insult to Balasaheb would not be tolerated. The row emerged after Shiv Sena protested against the distribution of Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, alleging it contained objectionable references to Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar. Party leaders including Shaina NC, Sanjay Nirupam and Anand Dubey tore pages from the book during a press conference and demanded that publisher HarperCollins remove the passages on pages 201 and 443. Following this protest, Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) accused Shaina of tearing Bal Thackeray's photograph instead. She rejected the allegation, claimed the image was of Mani Shankar Aiyar, challenged leaders to prove it, and threatened legal action over what she called defamatory claims. Meanwhile, Congress leader Nana Patole described the incident as 'petty, low-level politics' and demanded an FIR, strict action and an apology, while Uddhav Sena's Sanjay Raut said Shaina should be 'publically flogged' for damaging Balasaheb's photo. Separately, Shinde condemned Rahul Gandhi for repeatedly targeting Savarkar in his memoir and denounced those who had abandoned Bal Thackeray's ideology.
items.title: Eknath Shinde Defends Shaina NC Amid Bal Thackeray Photo Row and Savarkar Book Controversy
